Changing the node type to `Control` makes the reference resolve **and** attach, matching how `Main.tscn:5` already uses this same script. `load_steps=2` stays correct (one `ext_resource`, no sub-resources).

## Evidence

`Broken.tscn` was the only dangling reference in the project — the other two scenes resolve cleanly:

- `Main.tscn` → `res://scripts/story_runtime.gd` — exists
- `VisualNovelPreview.tscn` → `res://assets/images/bg_study_day.png` — exists
- **`Broken.tscn` → `res://scripts/does_not_exist.gd` — was missing**

All three `.import` files and their `source_file`/`dest_files` are intact, so nothing else is missing.

## What I could not check

Two things you should confirm when the shell works:

1. **Runtime verification.** I never got `godot --headless` to run. The change is reasoned from the scene/script contents, not observed.
2. **Reachability.** `project.godot:6` sets `run/main_scene="res://Main.tscn"`, and nothing in the project references `Broken.tscn`. So `godot --headless --quit-after 60` will never load it — that command will look clean whether or not this fix is right. To actually exercise it, load the scene directly, e.g. a one-off script doing `ResourceLoader.load("res://Broken.tscn")`, or an `.import` pass first since no `.godot/` cache exists yet: `godot --headless --import`.
